text:
Alex Kim: Heads up — NF4 canary on cluster-us-west-2 is showing KV cache churn and a ~22% throughput drop over the last 30m. memory usage on some hosts spiked ~1.5GB.

Priya Rao: Repro? which image and kernel selector? :eyes: 

Alex Kim: rolling canary image: redwood-runtime:v4-nf4-20260314, selector=auto-kernel-v2. Observed on p4d and a subset of 8xA100 hosts. thread_ts=1735678901

perf-bot: Canary metrics (30m window): requests=12.6k, tokens=3.2M, p50=45ms (+10%), p95=260ms (+32%), throughput tokens/s -22%. KV cache hit rate dropped from 0.87 -> 0.62 for impacted hosts.

Jamal Ortiz: That's a big cache hit delta. Any change to prefix caching or eviction heuristics in this deploy?

Alex Kim: Not intentionally. The build bumped the microbatch packing and introduced a new kernel path for 4-bit matmul (quant4_hybrid) that uses a different KV layout. Suspecting fragmentation + scheduler change.

Priya Rao: Can you paste the perf profile (top hotspots) and the kernel callstack from one of the slow hosts?

Alex Kim: Sure — grabbed a brief sampling (perf and nvprof snapshot):

```
# perf top (sample)
30.2%  quant4_hybrid_matmul
12.8%  kv_cache_lookup
9.5%   batch_assembly
6.1%   host_memcpy_async
4.2%   scheduler_poll
```

nvprof excerpt:
```
quant4_matmul_kernel<<<...>>>  72.8ms
kv_load_kernel<<<...>>>        18.1ms
memcpy_htod_async              24.0ms
```

Marta: That quant4 kernel latency of 72ms is unexpected for small batches. Do we have size distribution shift? Maybe packing created many tiny microbatches.

perf-bot: Recent route distribution: 54% small seq (<64), 28% mid (64-256), 18% long (>256). Avg microbatch size dropped from 3.2 -> 1.7 since canary start.

Jamal Ortiz: So two factors: kernel slower for small microbatches, and KV churn increases misses because of different layout causing more fragmentation. Could be allocator interaction.

Priya Rao: Any GC/allocator logs? Did slab sizes change for 4-bit backends?

Alex Kim: Yes — allocator dump shows more slabs in small-size bins: slab_count_small +45%, fragmentation ratio up 12%. Also observed increased host->device memcpy wait times when eviction starts.

Marta: Hypothesis: quant4_hybrid path uses per-layer small-block packing that multiplied KV entries and made eviction thrash. Two mitigations: (1) force old kernel path for small microbatches; (2) increase KV slab bin for 4-bit to coarser buckets.

Priya Rao: Agree. Quick test: flip config to disable quant4_hybrid for seq<128 and enable legacy kernel. Also bump KV slab min to 8KB.

Alex Kim: Pushed a config canary: runtime flag --kernel-fallback=legacy-for-small, kv-slab-min=8k. Rolling to 3 hosts now.

perf-bot: Post-fix (10m after): p95 down to +12% vs baseline, throughput -6% (much improved). KV hit rate recovered to 0.82 on patched hosts. Memory spike stabilized.

Jamal Ortiz: Good. Need to instrument kernel path entry to log microbatch sizes and KV allocations for next deploy. Also add a perf test for the quant4 kernel on small batches (unit harness).

Marta: I'll open a follow-up PR to adjust allocator thresholds and add metric tags: quant_kernel=quant4_hybrid|legacy, microbatch_size bucket, kv_bin.

Priya Rao: Action items:
- Alex: keep the fallback flag rolling and collect 1h traces on 10 hosts (include nvprof and allocator dumps) (due: 2h)
- Marta: PR for allocator/metrics (due: EOD)
- Jamal: add microbatch unit perf tests + CI job (due: 48h)

Alex Kim: Noted. One more observation — calibration sweep we ran earlier had tiny changes to scale estimation for NF4. Could be impacting kernel tiling heuristics. Marking research task: calibration->tiling interaction.

Marta: Good catch. Add to research board. Also let's add a safety check in routing: if KV hit rate drops >10% in 10m, automatically roll to legacy kernel for affected hosts.

Priya Rao: Agree. I can prototype the route policy.

perf-bot: Thread closed? :white_check_mark:

Alex Kim: Leaving open until 1h stable window. Thanks everyone :rocket:
